# The Sky That Remembers Our Names

## Scripture

*"Lift up your eyes and look to the heavens: Who created all these? He who brings out the starry host one by one and calls forth each of them by name. Because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing."* — Isaiah 40:26

## Reflection

On a clear October night, if you find a dark enough spot, you can see the faint glow of the Andromeda Galaxy—a smudge of light that left home 2.5 million years ago. The photons striking your eyes tonight began their journey before humans existed. And yet they arrive, patient and punctual, carried across an impossible distance by the same faithfulness that holds every atom together.

Isaiah wrote to a people who felt forgotten—exiles who wondered if God had lost track of them. His answer wasn't a lecture but an invitation: *look up*. Count the stars if you can. The One who calls each by name has not mislaid a single one. Not one is missing.

Here is the tender logic of the universe: if God's attention is that meticulous with burning balls of gas across light-years of emptiness, how much more does He hold you? Your name is not lost in the crowd. Your sleepless night, your quiet grief, your unanswered question—none of it has slipped past His notice. The God who keeps galaxies in their orbits keeps you.

The Andromeda light proves something beautiful: faithfulness that began long before you were born will arrive exactly when it's needed.

## Prayer

Lord, when I feel small and forgotten, lift my eyes to the heavens You made. Thank You that the One who names every star knows my name and has never let me go. Quiet my anxious heart with the patience of Your creation, and help me trust that Your faithful light will always reach me. Amen.
